segments.title: 第37章 人終有一死
segments.content:
Chapter 37: All Men Must Die

Ten thousand yuan.

For the current Li Luo, this was quite a large sum of money.

Saying it like that seemed a bit shameful for a transmigrator.

But his family had just bought a house, taking on a mortgage of about one million yuan, with monthly payments of five or six thousand yuan.

The breakfast shop's monthly profits were enough to cover this expense, since the storefront was their own property, with no additional rent costs.

However, it was naturally for the best if he could help ease the family's mortgage pressure a little.

Unfortunately, after asking for more details, Li Luo learned that this writing contest would last for three months.

After the three months, there would be a judging period of about one month. By that estimate, he would have to wait until the end of the first semester of his first year of high school.

Holding onto the thought that something was better than nothing, Li Luo still expressed his gratitude to his editor, Qian Zhou, and took a glance at the subscription numbers in his dashboard.

One hour after the book went premium, the number of subscribers for the first paid chapter was 307.

According to a normal growth curve, by this time tomorrow, the number of subscribers would be somewhere between 1600 and 2000.

For a new book from a new author, this result was quite remarkable.

No wonder Qian Zhou had placed his hopes for the first premium-works-level book under his charge on Li Luo.

Looking at the numbers on his dashboard, Li Luo gradually felt at ease. He took out a calculator, tapped away, and calculated his approximate monthly earnings from royalties.

He ended up with a figure of around six thousand.

Just enough to cover the mortgage, basically.

But if his book's performance continued to grow, his monthly income would definitely be more than this.

Qian Zhou: Your results right now are excellent, trust me.

Qian Zhou: Keep writing until you hit one million words, and you'll get recommended to all sorts of third-party channels. Your sources of income will become very diverse.

Qian Zhou: Many authors might only earn a few thousand from our main site, but when the revenue from all the third-party channels is combined, it can reach around ten thousand. The total is very impressive.

Reading the editor's words, Li Luo suddenly realized something.

In his previous life, when he wrote web novels, the entire industry had anti-piracy measures in place, and an author's income mainly came from subscriptions from paying readers on the main site.

But now, in 2014, it was still an era of widespread online piracy.

Qidian Chinese Website not only had its own site's income but also distribution through various channels.

Although there were many freeloading readers on the main site due to piracy, if there were enough channels, a change in quantity would lead to a change in quality, and the income would still be substantial.

But he still had to slog through to one million words before getting on those channels... Li Luo glanced at the word count in his draft folder and figured he should take it slow.

There was no rush to make money.

Qian Zhou: Of course, you still have to attend high school. I suggest you focus on your studies and at least ensure your academics go smoothly so your family doesn't worry.

Chong Ran: Okay, editor. Thanks for the reminder.

After chatting with his editor, Li Luo was about to start writing when another QQ message popped up.

Li Luo clicked it open and saw it was from Xu Youyu.

SleepEarlyGrowTall: What's your one-hour subscription count?

Chong Ran: Over 300. What about you?

SleepEarlyGrowTall: 120...

Chong Ran: That's already very impressive.

SleepEarlyGrowTall: Not as impressive as you. I read your book. Both the pacing and the gratifying moments are very well written. I feel like my writing is still too artsy. Readers often complain to me about it.

"Yeah, right," Li Luo thought, scoffing internally as he read Xu Youyu's message.

Just a few days ago at the dinner table, you said my book was mediocre, and now online it has become "very well written"?

Chong Ran: Your book has its own unique style, which I also really like. You don't need to pay attention to the opinions of a few readers. Sticking to your own content is the only way to not lose your way.

Despite his internal complaints, Li Luo repeated the same words Xu Youyu had once said to him, sending them right back to her.

Writing a serialized web novel was just like that.

You would constantly face all sorts of criticism and interference from readers.

If you couldn't adjust your mentality to handle this, you were destined to not go far.

SleepEarlyGrowTall: Thank you for the encouragement, Master! I'm going to go write now.

Chong Ran: Okay.

Looking at the cute dialogue style of Xu Youyu on QQ, Li Luo couldn't help but smile, thinking that his senior's personality online and offline was quite different.

Was she playing the "moe gap" card with him?

Li Luo grumbled a bit, then collected his thoughts and began to write.

In the evening.

Ying Chanxi came home, dropped off her schoolbag, changed into a nice outfit, and called for Xu Youyu. The two girls then linked arms and happily went downstairs to buy groceries.

After spending a few days together, the relationship between Ying Chanxi and Xu Youyu had progressed rapidly.

Although for the past few days they had school until evening self-study ended at 8:30 PM, every time Ying Chanxi came back, she would ask Li Luo to make a late-night snack.

Xu Youyu would then shamelessly come over to get a share. The two girls would chat while they ate and quickly became good friends.

Today was Friday, and there was no evening self-study. Ying Chanxi rushed home right after class to go grocery shopping with Xu Youyu, planning to have Li Luo cook a lavish feast for dinner.

Just as Ying Chanxi and Xu Youyu went out together to buy groceries, Li Luo went to the kitchen to do some prep work, only to receive a call from his mom.

"Hey, Mom, what's up?"

"What are you doing?" Lin Xiuhong asked from the other end.

"Thinking of you, Mom," Li Luo said sweetly.

"Get lost." Lin Xiuhong rolled her eyes, but the corners of her mouth curled up involuntarily. "School starts the day after tomorrow, right? What time in the morning?"

"We just have to register before nine o'clock."

"Then your dad and I will close the shop the day after tomorrow. We'll get to your place at eight in the morning and take you to school."

"The First Affiliated High School is just across the street, I can go by myself," Li Luo said with a laugh. "You guys don't need to worry."

"Is that us worrying?" Lin Xiuhong said irritably. "You worked so hard to get into the First Affiliated High School. You can't stop your dad and me from going over to show off a bit?"

"Fine, fine," Li Luo replied in quick succession. "You two can come then. Is there anything else?"

"Nope... Oh right, there is one more thing." Lin Xiuhong thought for a moment, then said, "Do you still remember your uncle?"

"I do, what's wrong?"

"Your uncle is a member of that writers' association, right? I figured since your novel was good enough to get a contract, it must be well-written, so I recommended it to him to have a look."

"What?!" Li Luo shouted, so startled by his mom's words that he jumped on the spot, nearly hitting the ceiling.

"What's wrong?" Hearing his huge reaction, Lin Xiuhong was puzzled. "Your uncle is very knowledgeable. We'll have him give you some pointers, and you can learn from him."

"No, Mom, the stuff I write..." Li Luo began with difficulty, "might not be suitable for people of my uncle's generation to read."

"What's not suitable about it?" Lin Xiuhong looked strange, then said, "Anyway, I already told your uncle. We'll see when he has time to take a look for you. That's all, see you the morning after tomorrow."

After hanging up, Li Luo's eyes went gray as if devoid of life, his head buzzing.

When Ying Chanxi and Xu Youyu returned with the groceries and entered the kitchen, they saw his crestfallen appearance and immediately asked, "What's wrong with you?"

"Nothing." Li Luo forced a smile and let out a gloomy sigh. "I just died a little, that's all."
